paragraphs: You can use your iPhone, iPad or even your Apple Watch as a remote for your Apple TV. It’s a convenient feature when you’ve lost the remote in the couch cushions.

And even if your remote hasn’t gone missing entirely, sometimes it’s sitting on the table way over there and you don’t want to interrupt a show by asking for someone to pass it to you. Or maybe someone is intentionally hogging the remote, and you want to pause the video on the Apple TV yourself. Either way, it’s really easy to do from an iPhone or an Apple Watch.

The Apple TV‘s Siri Remote is small, sleek and maddeningly easy to lose in the couch cushions. Fortunately, the best replacement might already be in your pocket. Your iPhone doubles as a fully functional Apple TV remote, letting you navigate menus, control playback and — best of all — type passwords without painfully pecking them out on a tiny clickpad.
You can even use your Apple Watch to control the action. Once you know where to find these built-in controls, you may never bother hunting for the Apple TV’s physical remote again.

Note: Apple’s support document says the Remote app works only with “Apple TV 4K, Apple TV HD, and AirPlay-compatible smart TVs.” To use the Remote app with a smart TV, you need to add the TV to your Apple Home app and assign it to a room in your home.

To take advantage of this handy feature, you need to make sure your iPhone is on the same network as your Apple TV. If you’re using your personal devices set up in your own home, this is almost certainly already the case. If you’re at a friend’s house, be sure to get their Wi-Fi password before you angrily fumble around the Remote app and curse Cupertino.
If you’ve set up an Apple TV before, you should automatically have a Remote icon added to your iPhone’s Control Center.

On a newer iPhone (iPhone X, XS, XR, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16), you can pull down from the top right of the screen to open Control Center and tap the Remote icon. (If you don’t see the icon, tap and hold on the screen, tap Add a Control at the bottom, then add Remote to Control Center.)
